title: Trump names Stephen Miller chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles
dek: Days after Republicans lost Congress, the president is changing who runs his White House. Allies and opponents agree on what Miller stands for and disagree on whether that is good.
what: On Friday, 6 November 2026, President Trump announced on social media that Stephen Miller, now deputy chief of staff, will become chief of staff starting Monday, 9 November. The White House account posted the announcement. It says Susie Wiles, who he says has done an outstanding job, is moving to the Trump Political Operation.

CNBC and PBS report the change. PBS quotes Wiles saying that serving the president in the White House was the honor of a lifetime. Both outlets describe Miller as an architect of the administration's hard-line immigration policy who has been with Trump since the 2016 campaign. They place the change days after Democrats won control of Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections.

CNBC reports that Vice President JD Vance praised Miller and that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth posted "Patriots in control." It reports that House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries called Miller "a dangerous xenophobe and reckless extremist" and that Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said Trump "learned nothing from his historic defeat." Democratic Representative Robert Garcia, the incoming chair of the House Oversight Committee, issued a statement; I could not read its text.

CNN's headline says Trump is "furious" over the midterm results, citing sources. That is the outlet's sourcing and I could not confirm it. Why Trump made the change is not on the record beyond his own post.
why: A chief of staff controls access to the president, so the choice reads as a signal about the next two years. Supporters read a loyal ally taking charge. Opponents read a refusal to moderate after a loss.

worlds.name: Supporters of the president
worlds.sees: A long-serving ally who backs the president's agenda is being promoted, and Wiles is thanked and kept on the political side.

worlds.name: Democrats and critics
worlds.sees: The architect of the hard-line immigration agenda is being put in charge after a rejection at the polls, a sign that the president will not change course.

common: Established: Trump announced the change on 6 November, Miller starts 9 November, and Wiles moves to his political operation. Reported by outlets: Miller's role in immigration policy and the reactions quoted above. Not established: the reasons for the change, and whether it will change policy. Those rest on opinion and on unnamed sources.
next: Miller starts on Monday, 9 November. Who fills the deputy post and any further staff changes would be announced by the White House.
